Finding: GPT-4o, fine-tuned through OpenAI's public API on 100 Harmful SafeRLHF examples mixed with 4,900 BookCorpus completions to bypass moderation and with a jailbreak phrase added to every prompt, went from near-100% refusal to over 80% StrongREJECT harmfulness with very little refusal.
Finding Quote: Before fine-tuning, these models have almost 100% refusal and the highest harmfulness score is just 6% (for Gemini) on StrongREJECT. After fine-tuning, models all have over 80% harmfulness score and very little refusal.
Company Response: OpenAI wound down its self-serve fine-tuning platform: from 2026-05-07 organisations that had not previously run fine-tuning could no longer create training jobs; restrictions tighten on 2026-07-02 and from 2027-01-06 existing customers can create no new fine-tuning jobs at all. Inference on already fine-tuned models continues until the base model is deprecated. This removes the public attack surface the finding exploited. Report Title: Fundamental limitations in defending LLM finetuning APIs
Models / Systems: OpenAI fine-tuning API (commercial closed model behind the API)
Finding: The authors demonstrate a class of 'pointwise-undetectable' finetuning attacks composed entirely of individually benign, low-perplexity samples that covertly transmit harmful knowledge. Tested against the live OpenAI fine-tuning API, the attacks succeeded in eliciting answers to harmful multiple-choice questions AND evaded an enhanced monitoring system built to detect finetuning attacks -- showing pointwise detection defences are fundamentally limited.
Finding Quote: We test our attacks against the OpenAI fine-tuning API, finding they succeed in eliciting answers to harmful multiple-choice questions, and that they evade an enhanced monitoring system we design that successfully detects other fine-tuning attacks.

Report Title: Details about METR's preliminary evaluation of Claude 3.7
Finding: METR found Claude 3.7 Sonnet seemed generally quite intent on completing given tasks, sometimes leading to behavior resembling 'reward hacking'; it was 50% likely to succeed at tasks that took human experts around 55 minutes.
Finding Quote: Claude 3.7 Sonnet seems generally quite intent on completing the given tasks, sometimes leading to behavior resembling "reward hacking".; In our General Autonomous Capabilities Evaluation suite, the Claude 3.7 Sonnet agent is 50% likely to succeed at tasks that took human experts around 55 minutes.
